lead_headline: Hell or High Water Tiki relocates to RiNo after LoDo closure, joining six other openings today including Olive & Finch's largest location yet in Golden Triangle

restaurant.blurb: 6 opening leads, 4 closure leads today: Hell or High Water Tiki (RiNo relocation), Olive & Finch (Golden Triangle), Bandar Grill (Sunnyside), HOTDOG & JUICY (Southwest Plaza), Maryjane's Hideaway (Edgewater), The Flaming Grill (downtown). Closures: Mighty Colorado Burger (Arvada), Mojo-99 Burgers (Regis), two Dairy Queen repeats.

liquor.blurb: Zero new applications today, holding the 7-day total at 2,386 licenses after Monday's database flood subsides. The week's unprecedented 2,386-count (up 13,156% from prior week's 18) confirms a mass renewal sync or system event rather than organic filings. No meaningful individual applications detected in Tuesday's batch — the liquor license landscape remains in post-surge cleanup mode as April closes, with May likely to reset to historical ~20-30 weekly baselines once the database stabilizes.

reputation.blurb: 7 mentions yesterday extends the 7-day count to 47 across 14 sources — up 7% from last week's 44 and sustaining April's closing momentum above Q1 baselines. Instagram (11) edges out Facebook (10) as the week's top source, followed by Reddit (6), Denver Post (4), and Hoodline (3). Tuesday's coverage included City Cast Denver's LoDo nightlife piece, Hoodline's Greenwood Village office tower seizure story, and social chatter about Temple Denver's evolution and new scooter contracts. The steady 47-mention pace confirms media interest has plateaued near monthly averages as April wraps, with social platforms maintaining their dominance over traditional outlets.

subscriptions.blurb: Net +1 yesterday (3 new, 2 canceled) nudges MTD to +23 (+0.8/day) with 90-day net at +117. Tuesday's modest gain follows Monday's +1 recovery from Sunday's −13 churn spike that erased the prior week's momentum — the 7-day total now stands at −1 net (21 new, 22 canceled), down sharply from last week's +13 and confirming April's late-month rally has stalled. The recent two-week pattern shows Sunday's 17-cancellation wave reversed 10 days of steady growth, with MTD's +0.8/day pace now trailing YTD's +1.3/day baseline by 38%. Barring a surprise Wednesday surge, April will close below March's conversion rate as volatility replaces the quarter's earlier stability.
